/**
 * The events a generated view declares, and the `data-event` attribute that
 * names one on an element.
 *
 * A view never runs code in the browser. Instead it marks a button or a form
 * with `data-event="name"` or `data-event="name:arg"`, and declares each name
 * in its module's `interactions` export:
 *
 * - a `state` event runs the view's `reduce` and renders again, with no model
 *   call;
 * - a `message` event becomes a question from the person, carrying the
 *   element's form values as data.
 *
 * An event whose name the view did not declare is refused, wherever it comes
 * from.
 *
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
import * as Option from "effect/Option";
import * as Schema from "effect/Schema";
/**
 * The most interactions one view may declare.
 *
 * @category constants
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const maxDeclared = 32;
/**
 * The longest `arg` an event may carry, in UTF-16 code units.
 *
 * @category constants
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const maxArgLength = 256;
/**
 * The longest label a `message` interaction may carry.
 *
 * @category constants
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const maxLabelLength = 80;
const namePattern = /^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31}$/;
/**
 * An interaction's name: a lowercase letter, then up to 31 letters, digits,
 * `_` or `-`. It never contains `:`, which separates the name from its
 * argument in a `data-event` attribute.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Name = Schema.String.check(Schema.isPattern(namePattern));
/**
 * An event that changes the view's own state: the parent runs `reduce` and
 * renders again. It never calls a model.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const StateInteraction = Schema.Struct({ kind: Schema.Literal("state") });
/**
 * An event that becomes a question from the person. `label` is the question's
 * text, such as the label of the button that sent it.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const MessageInteraction = Schema.Struct({
    kind: Schema.Literal("message"),
    label: Schema.String.check(Schema.isMinLength(1), Schema.isMaxLength(maxLabelLength)),
});
/**
 * One declared interaction.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Interaction = Schema.Union([StateInteraction, MessageInteraction]);
/**
 * A view's `interactions` export: each event name it may send, and its kind.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Declared = Schema.Record(Schema.String, Interaction).check(Schema.isPropertyNames(Name), Schema.isMaxProperties(maxDeclared));
/**
 * The argument a `data-event="name:arg"` attribute carries.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Arg = Schema.String.check(Schema.isMaxLength(maxArgLength));
/**
 * One event a view sent: the declared name and the optional argument from its
 * `data-event` attribute. `reduce` receives exactly this.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Event = Schema.Struct({ name: Name, arg: Schema.optionalKey(Arg) });
const decodeEvent = Schema.decodeUnknownOption(Event);
/**
 * Reads a `data-event` attribute: `"name"` or `"name:arg"`. Everything after
 * the first `:` is the argument. A malformed name or an overlong argument is
 * `None`.
 *
 * @category parsing
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const parse = (attribute) => {
    const at = attribute.indexOf(":");
    return at === -1
        ? decodeEvent({ name: attribute })
        : decodeEvent({ name: attribute.slice(0, at), arg: attribute.slice(at + 1) });
};
/**
 * Writes the `data-event` attribute for an event: the inverse of {@link parse}.
 *
 * @category parsing
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const format = (event) => event.arg === undefined ? event.name : `${event.name}:${event.arg}`;
/**
 * The declared interaction an event names, or `None` when the view did not
 * declare it. Own properties only, so `constructor` or `__proto__` never
 * match.
 *
 * @category lookups
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const lookup = (declared, name) => name !== "constructor" && name !== "__proto__" && Object.hasOwn(declared, name)
    ? Option.some(declared[name])
    : Option.none();

/**
 * The frame a generated view shows in, written by the trusted page and never
 * by the model.
 *
 * A view's HTML never runs as script. The page shows it in
 * `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc>`: an opaque origin with no cookies,
 * storage or parent DOM. The frame's document carries a Content Security
 * Policy whose only script is the page's own runtime, pinned by its SHA-256
 * hash, and it forbids inline event handlers, every network fetch, plugins,
 * nested frames, workers, `<base>` and form submission.
 *
 * The runtime asks the page for the view's HTML over the bridge (see
 * `Bridge`), parses it inertly and copies only allowlisted elements and
 * attributes into the document. This module writes the document around it.
 *
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
import * as Base64 from "effect/encoding/Base64";
import { digestSync } from "@smthrs/crypto";
/**
 * The frame's `sandbox` attribute: scripts for the page's runtime, and
 * nothing else. No `allow-same-origin`, `allow-forms`, `allow-popups`,
 * `allow-downloads`, `allow-modals` or `allow-top-navigation`.
 *
 * @category constants
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const sandbox = "allow-scripts";
/**
 * The attribute on the frame document's `<html>` element that carries the
 * per-mount nonce for `ui/initialize`.
 *
 * @category constants
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const nonceAttribute = "data-smithers-nonce";
/**
 * A script's CSP source expression: `'sha256-<base64>'` over its UTF-8 text.
 *
 * @category hashing
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const hash = (script) => {
    const hex = digestSync(script);
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(32);
    for (let index = 0; index < 32; index++)
        bytes[index] = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(index * 2, index * 2 + 2), 16);
    return `'sha256-${Base64.encode(bytes)}'`;
};
/**
 * The frame's policy for a runtime with the given {@link hash}.
 *
 * `script-src-attr 'none'` blocks inline event handlers even where a
 * sanitizer missed one. `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` admits the page's theme
 * sheet and React's `style` attributes; `img-src` and `font-src` admit only
 * `data:` URLs, so nothing in a view reaches the network.
 *
 * @category policies
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const policy = (runtimeHash) => [
    "default-src 'none'",
    `script-src ${runtimeHash}`,
    "script-src-attr 'none'",
    "style-src 'unsafe-inline'",
    "img-src data:",
    "font-src data:",
    "connect-src 'none'",
    "media-src 'none'",
    "object-src 'none'",
    "frame-src 'none'",
    "child-src 'none'",
    "worker-src 'none'",
    "manifest-src 'none'",
    "base-uri 'none'",
    "form-action 'none'",
].join("; ");
/** Keeps a script or style sheet from closing its own element early. */
const inert = (text, tag) => text.replace(new RegExp(`</(${tag})`, "gi"), "<\\/$1");
const attribute = (value) => value.replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/"/g, """).replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">");
/**
 * The frame's `srcdoc`: the policy, the page's styles and the runtime, and no
 * view content. The view's HTML arrives later over the bridge. The runtime is
 * the body's only child, so the body exists when it runs.
 *
 * The runtime is hashed exactly as it is written into the document, after any
 * `</script` in it is escaped, so the policy always admits it.
 *
 * @category documents
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const frameDocument = (options) => {
    const runtime = inert(options.runtime, "script");
    return `<!doctype html><html ${nonceAttribute}="${attribute(options.nonce)}" data-theme="${attribute(options.theme)}"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="${attribute(policy(hash(runtime)))}"><meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer"><style>${inert(options.styles, "style")}</style></head><body><script>${runtime}</script></body></html>`;
};
